items.front: Immediate cause of the 1857 Revolt?
items.back: Greased Enfield rifle cartridges (cow + pig fat), which had to be bitten — offended Hindus and Muslims.

items.front: Mangal Pandey — where and when?
items.back: Attacked officers at Barrackpore on 29 March 1857 (34th Native Infantry); hanged 8 April 1857.

items.front: When did open revolt break out and where did it head?
items.back: Meerut, 10 May 1857 (85 sepoys jailed 9 May); sepoys marched to Delhi and proclaimed Bahadur Shah Zafar II leader.

items.front: Centre–leader pairs (1857)?
items.back: Delhi–Bahadur Shah Zafar/Bakht Khan; Kanpur–Nana Sahib/Tatya Tope; Lucknow–Begum Hazrat Mahal; Jhansi–Rani Lakshmi Bai; Arrah–Kunwar Singh.

items.front: Fate of Bahadur Shah Zafar?
items.back: Delhi recaptured 20 Sept 1857; he was exiled to Rangoon, sons executed. Tatya Tope executed 1859.

items.front: Why did the revolt fail?
items.back: Limited to North India; no unified leadership/ideology; superior British arms + telegraph; loyal princely states (Gwalior, Indore, Hyderabad, Sikhs).
items.examPoint: Reasons for the failure of the revolt

items.front: Chief consequence — the 1858 Act?
items.back: Government of India Act 1858 ended EIC rule, transferred India to the Crown; created Secretary of State for India; Canning = first Viceroy.
items.examPoint: Government of India Act 1858 — end of Company rule

items.front: Queen's Proclamation 1858 promised?
items.back: Non-interference in religion, equal opportunity in appointments (not fully honoured), recognition of princes' rights, end to annexations.

items.front: Peel Commission did what to the army?
items.back: Raised British:Indian troop ratio; segregated units by caste/region; barred Indians from artillery; recruited more Sikhs/Gurkhas.

items.front: What does 'Ulgulan' mean and who led it?
items.back: 'Great Tumult' = Birsa Munda's Munda rebellion (1899–1900), Chotanagpur. Birsa honoured on Janjatiya Gaurav Divas (15 Nov).
items.examPoint: Tribal & peasant uprisings — Ulgulan (Birsa Munda), Santhal Hul, Kol, Sanyasi, Indigo

items.front: Santhal Hul — years, leaders, aftermath?
items.back: 1855–56, led by Sidhu & Kanhu; British created the Santhal Parganas and banned Santhal→non-Santhal land transfer.
items.examPoint: Tribal & peasant uprisings — Ulgulan (Birsa Munda), Santhal Hul, Kol, Sanyasi, Indigo

items.front: Why did indigo cultivation decline?
items.back: Synthetic (aniline) dyes made natural indigo unprofitable by the early 20th c. Indigo Revolt 1859–60; Neel Darpan (1860).

items.front: Who called 1857 the 'First War of Independence'?
items.back: V.D. Savarkar; the British called it a 'Sepoy Mutiny'.

items.front: Andhra & 1857? Rayalaseema precursor?
items.back: Deccan/Ceded Districts stayed quiet; Nizam backed the British. Precursor: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy's revolt (1846–47), hanged at Koilkuntla 1847.
items.examPoint: Uyyalawada Narasimha Reddy revolt (1846-47) — Rayalaseema precursor
